messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming/v1 endpoints p99 latency breached 1200ms for last 3m (SLO=800ms). Error spike on tail tokens. Auto-annotation: suspected KV cache pressure.

sara: seeing it on the dashboard too. p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 1.25s. Streaming stalls increasing.

miguel: any customer-facing incidents yet?

emily_support: one customer (acme-inc) reported timeouts on live chat integrations ~5m ago, CS is triaging.

anika: looking at kv-metrics, eviction-rate spiked x3, slab_free dropped to 8%. Prefill queue length up ~600. Prefill vs decode skew: prefill processing much slower than decode.

lee: copy. can someone dump recent logs for prefill workers?

anika: pasted tail of prefill logs:
```
[2026-03-15T10:34:12Z] prefill-worker-12 WARN decode-slow id=xyz prefill_ms=980 decode_ms=120
[2026-03-15T10:34:20Z] kv-cache INFO eviction triggered slab=3 keys=1456
[2026-03-15T10:34:25Z] prefill-worker-8 ERROR failed_to_prefill timeout
```

sara: that 980ms prefill is the issue. Streaming requests hit hot prefixes and wait on prefill -> tail stalls. Looks like KV fragmentation causing many small reads and eviction churn.

miguel: can we reduce prefill concurrency for streaming route or temporarily disable prefill for low-priority models?

ops-bot: suggested runbook step: "throttle_prefill_for_route streaming/v1 to 0.3x" available via config flag `prefill.concurrency.multiplier`.

sara: I'm going to apply conservative throttle and increase KV slab reclaim threshold. Doing the change now.

sara: `kubectl -n infra exec -it config-manager -- /bin/sh -c "set-prefill-multiplier streaming/v1 0.3 && set-kv-slab-reclaim 0.15"`

ops-bot: command accepted, rolling config update to prefill-controller and kv-manager (3 pods).

anika: also bumping KV node count by +1 to reduce eviction pressure: `infractl scale kv-cluster --add-nodes 1`

ops-bot: scale job queued, expected 90s to join.

sara: after throttling: p99 dropped from 1250ms -> 820ms in ~45s. Prefill queue depth reduced to ~120. Eviction-rate trending down.

miguel: good. any regressions on throughput?

anika: throughput slightly lower for streaming (~6%), but latency improved. Customers should see fewer stalls.

emily_support: notifying affected customers: ACME, Streamly, BotShop; message drafted and ready to send if we hold steady 10m.

lee: we should also enable a temporary bypass: for streaming requests with model=fast-chat, skip prefill and fallback to partial-prefix decode. Patch ready: `routes.v1.stream.skip_prefill=true` (canary on 10% first).

sara: deploying skip_prefill=10% canary on two regions now.

ops-bot: canary applied to us-east-1 and eu-west-1 at 10%. Monitoring health.

anika: telemetry shows canary hosts behave normally, p99 for canary 460ms vs control 800ms. No error increases.

miguel: nice. plan: keep prefill throttled, allow KV node to stabilize (10m), and expand canary to 50% if steady. I'll take ownership for next 2 hours to monitor.

sara: handing off to miguel for 2h. Key actions taken: 1) prefill multiplier -> 0.3; 2) kv-cluster +1 node; 3) kv-slab-reclaim -> 0.15; 4) skip_prefill canary 10% on fast-chat.

miguel: acknowledged. I'll watch p95/p99, eviction-rate, and prefill queue. If p99 < 800ms and eviction-rate down, graduate canary.

oliver_pm: from product side — any risk to model quality from skipping prefill on canary?

anika: minor degradation potential for edge-long-context cases, but fast-chat fallback provides graceful decoding. We'll add a quick eval on top-50 prompts to ensure no major regressions.

emily_support: sending interim update to affected customers now: noted mitigations and ETA 30-60m for full recovery.

miguel: next steps timeline: monitor 30m -> if stable, increase skip_prefill to 50% and reduce prefill throttle to 0.5. If metrics regress, rollback skip_prefill immediately and re-evaluate KV tuning.

sara: marking incident as live-mitigation. tagging oncall-next: @miguel. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident thread created: 6132100000. Severity P1 -> P2 (mitigations applied). Logging handoff to Miguel for 2h.

miguel: taking over — ping me on this thread for any alerts, I'll escalate to infra immediately if we see eviction-rate > baseline*1.5.

sara: thanks team. I'll follow up with a short postmortem draft after we verify stability.

emily_support: customer notifications sent, will update on replies.

lee: leaving a note: consider longer-term: defragmentation job + hotspot-aware partitioning, and better prefill backpressure to avoid prefills starving decode.

anika: agreed — opening a follow-up ticket: IMPL-5243 (KV defrag + prefill backpressure).

miguel: handing off to oncall rotation at 12:40Z (2h). Leaving monitoring queries pinned.

sara: thanks all.
